auren.name: Auren
auren.story: Auren are mysterious forest-dwelling people that are said to exist without a physical body. Unfortunately, one cannot prove this as you will never get to see them when wandering through the woods. When threatened or expecting relatives to visit, they simply blend with the trees and become invisible.
auren.stronghold_1_built_special_action: After building the Stronghold, immediately and only once get 1 Favor tile. As a Special action (once per Action phase), you may advance 2 spaces on a Cult track of your choice (or on space 10 if you have a key).

witches.name: Witches
witches.story: Witches live in the woods, but they also dominate the air. Riding their brooms, they fly from place to place. This is why a forest that has never seen a Witch before all of a sudden may become full of Witches. Witches are sociable, so they gladly join up in large Witch towns, where they keep trading love potions and portable curses with each other.
witches.stronghold_1_built_special_action: After building the Stronghold, as a Special action (once per Action phase), you may build 1 Dwelling on an unoccupied Forest space. Neither pay 1 Worker, nor 2 Coins for this Dwelling. For this build only, ignore the adjacency rule. You may build on any free Forest space as long as it has been Forest at the beginning of this Action (Witches’ Ride).
witches.faction_ability: Get 5 additional Victory points when founding a Town

fakirs.name: Fakirs
fakirs.story: Fakirs have reduced their physical needs to a minimum and tremendously improved their spiritual forces. Their spirit rules over matter in such a way that they are able to levitate things like carpets. Carpets are very convenient flying devices when you know how to operate them. In contrast to brooms, they are capable of transporting load. Fakirs prefer to live in deserts as these comply with their meditative lifestyle due to the desert's considerable lack of plants and animals.
fakirs.stronghold_1_built_effect: After building the Stronghold, you may now skip 2 Terrain, or 2 River spaces, or one each when doing a Carpet Flight. (This also affects the final Area scoring.)
fakirs.faction_ability: When taking the „Transform and Build“ action, you may skip one Terrain or River space by paying 1 more Priest (Carpet Flight). Get 4 Victory points each time when doing a Carpet Flight. In the final Area scoring, any Structures that can be reached via Carpet Flight are considered connected (regardless of the number of your leftover Priests).

nomads.name: Nomads
nomads.story: Nomads are a horse people of the desert. They used to be living in tents and always on the move. Even today, they build their dwellings using plain and light materials. This way they can populate large areas really quickly. Nomads only dwell in deserts, and their hordes of horsemen can cause a sand storm that may propagate to neighboring landscapes.
nomads.stronghold_1_built_special_action: As a Special action (once per Action phase), you may transform a Terrain space directly adjacent to one of your Structures into your Home terrain (Sandstorm). On this space, you may immediately build a Dwelling by paying its costs. (This ability is not applicable past a River space or Bridge.)
nomads.faction_ability: You start the game with 3 instead of 2 Dwellings. Place the third one after all players have placed their second ones (but before the Chaos Magicians have placed their only Dwelling).

chaosmagicians.name: Chaos Magicians
chaosmagicians.story: Chaos Magicians appreciate the forces of destruction and feel the best when in dismal wastelands. They worship fire and are always looking for underground lava streams that they try to force to erupt and hit the surface to transform even more land into wasteland. Chaos Magicians also have a certain power over time – they are able to freeze time for other people so they can wreak havoc undisturbed.
chaosmagicians.stronghold_1_built_special_action: After building the Stronghold, as a Special action (once per Action phase), you may take a double-turn. (On this double-turn, take any 2 Actions one after another – passing is also considered an Action.)
chaosmagicians.faction_ability: You start the game with only one Dwelling. You may only place this Dwelling after all the other players have build all of theirs (if necessary, after the Nomads have placed their third one). You get 2 Favor tiles instead of 1 whenever you build a Temple or your Sanctuary.

giants.name: Giants
giants.story: Giants are beings of enormous size and physical strength. They can pull out trees or level out mountains with ease – as a matter of fact, they actually enjoy it. They are able to transform any landscape into wasteland in no time. Various Giants have already tried to transform land into something else, but it ended up being wasteland anyway. Apparently, they simply have no knack for the finer things.
giants.stronghold_1_built_special_action: After building the Stronghold, as a Special action (once per Action phase), get 2 free Spades to transform a reachable Terrain space into your Home terrain. On this space, you may immediately build a Dwelling by paying its costs.
giants.faction_ability: You always pay exactly 2 Spades to transform a Terrain space into your Home terrain - even for Mountains and Desert. (A single Spade will be forfeit when gained as a Cult bonus.)

swarmlings.name: Swarmlings
swarmlings.story: From all the factions, Swarmlings are the most sociable one. They simply cannot bear loneliness. They always wander about in large groups, being in water most of the time, yet they get along on land just as well. And when a Swarmling needs a work done, he may be assured of the help from friends and relatives who will give strong support. This way they even get the toughest work done.
swarmlings.stronghold_1_built_special_action: After building the Stronghold, as a Special action (once per Action phase), you may upgrade a Dwelling to a Trading house. Neither pay Coins, nor Workers for this Trading house.
swarmlings.faction_ability: Collect 3 additional Workers when founding a Town.

mermaids.name: Mermaids
mermaids.story: Mermaids are lovely water creatures inhabiting the waters of Terra Mystica and traveling by its rivers. Deceived by their charm, many a landsman has forgotten that the Mermaids preferably would like to transform Terra Mystica into a world of water. Mermaids are able to split their fishtail into two legs and traverse through land; however, they only do so when going to flood it with water, or when they need building materials for their floating cities.
mermaids.stronghold_1_built_effect: After building the Stronghold, immediately and only once move forward 1 space on the Shipping track. Neither pay 1 Priest, nor 4 Coins for this movement. (Take the rewards associated with the new level as indicated on your Faction board.)
mermaids.faction_ability_action: You may skip one River space when founding a Town. (You decide if and when you want to use this ability. When founding a Town in this fashion, put the Town tile on the skipped River space. Of course, you may build Bridges as usual.)

dwarves.name: Dwarves
dwarves.story: Dwarves are always on a hunt for treasures and valuable ores, thus engage in, non-stop burrowing in soil. Their mines are usually located in the mountains, but in the heat of digging, they sometimes end up digging underneath a neighboring area. Even if this is inhabited, its inhabitants most often will only notice when the Dwarves all of a sudden appear on the other side of that area. Dwarves go through so much soil that they are able to form new mountains from the spoil, so that future generations of Dwarves may dig through these all over again.
dwarves.stronghold_1_built_effect: After building the Stronghold, only pay 1 more Worker instead of 2 when Tunneling.
dwarves.faction_ability: When taking the „Transform and Build“ action, you may skip one Terrain or River space by paying 2 more Workers (Tunneling). Get 4 Victory points each time when Tunneling. You have no Shipping. In the final Area scoring, any Structures that can be reached via Tunneling are considered connected (regardless of the number of your leftover Workers).

engineers.name: Engineers
engineers.story: Initially, Engineers have been a mountain tribe living in inaccessible valleys and ravines. They have learned how to build bridges and mountain roads to keep their remote settlements connected. They enjoy dominating nature by means of technology. They appear eccentric to the other factions when poring over their construction plans.
engineers.stronghold_1_built_effect: After building the Stronghold, each round when passing, get 3 Victory points for each Bridge connecting two of your Structures.
engineers.faction_ability_action: As an Action, you may build a Bridge for 2 Workers. (You may take this Action any number of times during a round. You may still build Bridges via the respective Power action.)

halflings.name: Halflings
halflings.story: Halflings are nice little guys, not overly strong, intelligent, or apt in magic. So, hard work is their only way to achieve something in life. And with hard work, they achieve amazing things. Wherever a family of Halflings appears, the landscape will become flourishing farmland in a heartbeat – and this with only their own hands' work.
halflings.stronghold_1_built_effect: After building the Stronghold, immediately and only once get 3 Spades to apply on Terrain spaces following the general rules. You may build a Dwelling on exactly one of these spaces by paying its costs.
halflings.faction_ability: Get 1 additional Victory point for each Spade you get throughout the game (regardless of the way you get the Spade).

cultists.name: Cultists
cultists.story: Cultists love rituals. Their entire life is based on strict rules. Even the simplest things are accompanied by secret symbols and invocations of the elements. For instance, when a Cultist wants to fill a bucket of water from a well, he first needs to appease the elements of earth and water which he is tearing apart, then he also needs to ensure the element of fire that he is not going to extinguish it with that water. This may seem overly elaborate, but the Cultists also greatly benefit from the power of the elements.
cultists.stronghold_1_built_effect: After building the Stronghold, immediately and only once get 7 Victory points.
cultists.faction_ability: Whenever at least one of your opponents decides to take Power due to your building activity, advance 1 space on a Cult track of your choice. (You only get to advance 1 space in total regardless of the number of opponents taking Power. If all of your opponents refuse to take Power, do not advance on a Cult track, instead gain exactly one Power.)

alchemists.name: Alchemists
alchemists.story: Alchemists strive for a deeper knowledge of the elements forming the world and how to use them for their purposes. They know how to create gold – the process, however, is very elaborate and is only worth its while when you really need that gold. Alchemists prefer to settle in Swamps as these provide a steady supply of sulfur and other reagents.
alchemists.stronghold_1_built_effect: After building the Stronghold, immediately and only once gain 12 Power. From now on, gain 2 Power for each Spade you get throughout the remainder of the game (regardless of the way you get the Spade).
alchemists.faction_ability_action: You may trade 1 Victory point for 1 Coin, or 2 Coins for 1 Victory Point anytime and any number of times (Sorcerer’s Stone).

darklings.name: Darklings
darklings.story: Darklings are said to be wicked and smarmy creatures that lure others into dangerous marshy hollows for fun, only to rob and then drown them. Only few have tried to verify these rumors. Darklings are fairly skilled in the elemental cults – that's for sure. Their priests use their secret knowledge to bog even more land.
darklings.stronghold_1_built_effect: After building the Stronghold, you may immediately and only once trade up to 3 Workers for 1 Priest each (Ordination of Priests).
darklings.faction_ability: You need to pay Priests (instead of Workers) when transforming Terrain spaces. Pay 1 Priest and get 2 Victory points for each step of transformation.

chashdallah.name: Chash Dallah
chashdallah.stronghold_1_built_effect: After building the Stronghold: you can use power actions by paying money instead of power. You cannot mix paying both power and money, the whole cost has to be paid in either power or money.
chashdallah.faction_ability_action: Chash Dallah have an additional income track for income of coins and workers. That income is cumulative. They go up to a maximum 6 coins and 2 workers. Cost of advancement is 2 coins and 2 workers. They gain 1/2/3/4 VPs for advancement.

theenlightened.name: The Enlightened
theenlightened.stronghold_1_built_special_action: After building the Stronghold, when converting power into priests, workers or coins, you gain double the amount. As a special action, you may gain 4 power.
theenlightened.faction_ability: The Enlightened can convert 1 coin into an additional power token in bowl I.

archivists.name: Archivists
archivists.stronghold_1_built_effect: After building the Stronghold: when passing, you can pick 2 Round boosters instead of 1.
archivists.faction_ability: Archivists do not gain any cult bonuses at end of round (the reward on the right side of the round scoring tile). When passing and picking a new Round booster (or 2 with Stronghold), they gain 2 power for each coin on that Round booster(s) they pick.

djinni.name: Djinni
djinni.stronghold_1_built_effect: After building the Stronghold: when passing gain 1 VP per priest in a cult.
djinni.faction_ability_action: Djinni start the game with 3 magical lamps. As an action, you may spend one of your magical lamps to swap the position of 2 of your cult markers within your cults (e.g. when you are at 1 step in fire and 6 steps in air cult before the swap, you are at 6 steps in fire and 1 step in air afterwards). No power is gained by that swap.

treasurers.name: Treasurers
treasurers.stronghold_1_built_effect: After building the Stronghold, you may place priests, coins and workers into your Safe at any time, not just during income phase. So you can also put in resources you get from Power Actions, Town tiles or Cult Rewards. You can only put in resources the moment you receive them.
treasurers.faction_ability: Priests, coins and workers the Treasurers gain as income can go into their Safe instead of their supply. At the start of the income phase of each turn (so before regular income), they gain double of what is in the Safe (e.g. in round 1, they choose to put 2 workers in the Safe instead of their supply, then in round 2 they gain 4 workers before income).

architects.name: Architects
architects.stronghold_1_built_special_action: After building the Stronghold: as a special action, you may move 1 already built bridge to a different position where you could build a bridge. You gain 3 VPs when using this action. You may not remove a bridge that would leave a town marker in an area that does not qualify for a town anymore. You may remove a bridge from a town though if afterwards the marker is still in an area qualifying for a town (so you can grow a town and then split it into 2 towns). When moving a bridge, check if any town marker on either side of the old or new location of the bridge is affected by it. Each town marker still needs to be supported by a sufficient number and power value of buildings (and/or bridges). If the move of the bridge would make 2 (or more) town markers part of the same town, the town needs to have a sufficient number and power value of buildings to support ALL town markers. So for example, joining 2 town markers means you need 8 buildings with a power value of 14 (or 7 buildings of the Sanctuary is part of the town).
architects.faction_ability_action: As an action, Architects may spend 1 priest to build a bridge. Bridges count as 1 power (but not a separate building) towards the 7 power needed for a town. When the Architects transform and build over a bridge (but not when they just transfom, without building) they need 1 spade less to transform for each bridge connected to that space (so not a free spade, you dont get 2 VP in a spade scoring round for this).

atlanteans.name: Atlanteans
atlanteans.stronghold_1_built_effect: When your initial Stronghold town grows to certain power levels (similar to the 7 power you need to build a regular town) you get an immediate one-time bonus (this can happen by connecting another town): ${bulleted} 7 power: a free shipping advance ${bulleted} 10 power: advance 2 steps in each cult ${bulleted} 16 power: gain 20 VPs.
atlanteans.faction_ability_action: You start the game with only a Stronghold instead of 2 Dwellings. You may only place this Stronghold after all the other players have build all of theirs. Your Stronghold immediately forms a town. As an Action, you may build a Bridge for 2 Workers. (You may take this Action any number of times during a round. You may still build Bridges via the respective Power action.)

wisps.name: Wisps
wisps.stronghold_1_built_effect: After building the Stronghold, you may immediately place a free Dwelling on any water space anywhere on the map.
wisps.faction_ability: Whenever the Wisps build a Trading House, they may immediately terraform adjacent spaces with 1 spade. They may not build there immediately.

dyniongeifr.name: Dynion Geifr
dyniongeifr.stronghold_1_built_effect: After building the Stronghold, you immediatly gain 2 priests. You can found a town including the Stronghold with only 3 buildings (akin to the ability of every Sanctuary).
dyniongeifr.faction_ability: Whenever Dynion Geifr convert 1 priest into 1 worker, they get 1 extra worker and 2 coins. They also start with the Fire2 favor.

conspirators.name: Conspirators
conspirators.stronghold_1_built_special_action: After building the Stronghold, you immediatly gain 1 Favor tile. As a special action, you can put one of your Favor tiles back into the supply to get a different Favor tile from the supply. For the Favor tile you return, move back the corresponding cult steps, but do not gain or lose power for that. You also do not lose anything else you gained from the Favor, like a town you founded with 6 power worth of buildings. For the new Favor tile gain cult steps (and power if applicable) normally.
conspirators.faction_ability: When gaining a Favor tile, Conspirators receive 2 coins.

golddiggers.name: Prospectors
golddiggers.stronghold_1_built_special_action: After building the Stronghold, the cost to buy a golden spade is reduced to 3 coins. As a special action, you can gain 1 coin per Trading House of other players (e.g. the other players have a combined 4 Trading Houses in play, you get 4 coins).
golddiggers.faction_ability: Instead of regular spades, Prospectors get priests. To terraform, they use golden spades, which they can buy for 4 coins each. Every time they buy a golden spade, they also get 1 power and 1 VP (victory point).

timetravellers.name: Time Travellers
timetravellers.stronghold_1_built_special_action: After building the Stronghold: As a special action, you can move up to 4 power tokens from bowl I into bowl III.
timetravellers.faction_ability: The Time Travellers do not use the round scoring of the current round scoring tile. Instead, they gain points for BOTH the round scoring time from the previous round AND the next round. For that purpose, treat the round scoring tiles from rounds 1 and 6 as adjacent (time as a circle). If both round scoring tiles show the same reward, they gain both of them (so for example 4 VP for building a Dwelling in round 2 when both the scoring tiles from 1 and 3 give 2 VP each for building a Dwelling). They gain cult rewards at end of round normally (using the current round tile as everyone else).

goblins.name: Goblins
goblins.stronghold_1_built_effect: After building the Stronghold: whenever you gain a town marker, you gain an additional special marker.
goblins.faction_ability_action: Goblins start with 1 special marker. Whenever you build a Temple or Sanctuary, you gain 1 additional special marker (in addition to the Favor tile). As an action, you may spend one of your special markers to decide on a kind of structure and then get a reward based on how many of those structures you have on the board: ${bulleted} Per Dwelling: 1 power ${bulleted} Per Trading House: 2 coins ${bulleted} Per Temple: 1 worker ${bulleted} Per Stronghold: 1 cult step and/or per Sanctuary: 2 cult steps

childrenofthewyrm.name: Children Of The Wyrm
childrenofthewyrm.stronghold_1_built_special_action: After building the Stronghold, you immediately get back all power tokens you sacrificed so far. As a special action, you can now sacrifice up to 2 power tokens and place them on the Map. Place them, one after the other, onto a river hex which must be either directly adjacent to one of your buildings or one of your other tokens. Any hex and any building, that is directly adjacent to one of those power tokens, counts as directly adjacent to all of your buildings that are directly adjacent to that same power token or any power token that is connected to it FOR THE CHILDREN OF THE WYRM ONLY.
childrenofthewyrm.faction_ability: The Children of the Wyrm have to pay 1 less Victory Point whenever they leech. So they can leech 1 or 2 power for free, 3 power for 1 VP and so on. All of their buildings have different coin costs in the same way as every factions Trading Houses have. So you pay the lower amount of coins when there is at least 1 other factions building directly adjacent and the higher cost if there is not. Also whenever they sacrifice a power token in bowl II, they can move up to 2 other power tokens from bowl II to bowl III, not just 1.

auren.name: Tree of Serenity
auren.description: Once the Tree of Serenity is placed, every time the Auren advance to space 10 of a Cult, they get 4 Victory points.

witches.name: Raven's Blunder
witches.description: When Raven's Blunder is placed, every time the Witches found a new Town, they must choose between gaining 5 Victory points as usual or advancing 3 steps on a Cult track of their choice.

alchemists.name: Gloomy Workshop
alchemists.description: After placing the Gloomy Workshop, the Alchemists may immediately and only once do both, advance on the Shipping track and/or lower the Exchange rate for Spades, without paying the Priest cost. They must pay the other resources; and they gain Victory points as usual.

darklings.name: Camp
darklings.description: The Camp counts as a Dwelling (so tiles providing Victory points for Dwellings also provide them for the Camp). The Camp cannot be upgraded.

cultists.name: Cult Palace
cultists.description: The Cult Palace does not provide any additional benefit during the game. During Cult Scoring, the Cultists break ties, i.e. they are supposed to be half a step ahead of where they actually are in each Cult.

halflings.name: Driller
halflings.description: The Halflings pay a total of 1 fewer Spade (but at least 1) every time they transform a Terrain space that is directly adjacent to the Driller.

dwarves.name: Great Tunnel
dwarves.description: With the Great Tunnel as the starting point, the Dwarves may Tunnel through 2 Terrain spaces instead of just 1. Every time they get Spades as a Cult Bonus, they may Tunnel to spend these Spades. They do not pay Workers for that Tunneling but do not gett victory point for it.

engineers.name: Bridge Tower
engineers.description:
When the Bridge Tower is placed, the Engineers gain the ability to build so-called Land Bridges.

A Land Bridge must start at one of the six corners of the Bridge Tower and leads along the shared edge of the two Terrain spaces adjacent to that corner.

The Engineers must place an actual Bridge piece on that edge. It does not matter whether or not one of these Terrain spaces is a River space; and it does not matter whether or not one or both of these Terrain spaces are occupied by Structures (regardless of whose Structures they are). For instance, a Land Bridge may allow the Engineers to ”break through“ an impassible barrier of opponent Structures.

Land Bridges do not interfere with the adjacency of the Structures on the bordering Terrain spaces.

Land Bridges count as normal Bridges with regard to the Bridge scoring once the Stronghold is built (i.e. they provide 3 Victory points if the condition for that is met).

mermaids.name: Coral Reef
mermaids.description: The Coral Reef must be placed on a River space that is directly adjacent to a Mermaid Structure. It does not prevent other players from using that River space for expansion or indirect adjacency. Shipping works from the Coral Reef as with any other Structure. When founding a town containing the Coral Reef, the Coral Reef is the skipped river space.
mermaids.specialcost: 1 Spade (nota bene: Special Landscapes cannot be placed during the Cult Bonus phase)

swarmlings.name: Breeding Ground
swarmlings.description:
Breeding Ground allows a Town to grow even bigger while gaining additional Town tiles:

• At a total Power value of 14, the Town becomes a City, gaining its second Town tile.
• At a total Power value of 21, the City becomes a Metropolis, gaining its third Town tile.
• At a total Power value of 28, the Metropolis becomes a Megacity, gaining its fourth Town tile.

With the appropriate Favor tile (”2 Fire“), these values decrease to 12, 18, and 24, respectively.

chaosmagicians.name: Chaos Portal
chaosmagicians.description: When the Chaos Magicians build their Stronghold, they may immediately place the Chaos Portal on a free Wasteland space of their choice, anywhere on the game board.

giants.name: Cave of Wisdom
giants.description: When the Cave of Wisdom is placed, the Giants may immediately and only once lower the Exchange rate for Spades at no cost by moving their marker on the Exchange track up one space. If they do, they gain the normal 6 Victory points.

fakirs.name: Flight School
fakirs.description: When the Flight School is placed, the Fakirs get 2 Coins every time they use their Carpet Flight.

nomads.name: Trading Camp
nomads.description: Every time another player builds next to the Trading Camp, the Nomads may either take Power at the normal rate or take exactly 1 Coin from the general supply. If they take the Coin, they do not lose any Victory points.

icemaidens.name: Winterfall
icemaidens.description: When Winterfall is placed, the Ice Maidens get 1 Spade every time they build a Temple. When they do, they must spend the Spade immediately.

yetis.name: Frozen Peak
yetis.description: When the Frozen Peak is placed, the Yetis may immediately and only once place 2 Power tokens from the general supply in Bowl III.

dragonlords.name: Lava Pond
dragonlords.description: When the Lava Pond is placed, at the start of every round, the Dragonlords may place 1 Power token from the general supply in Bowl III.

acolytes.name: Altar of Sacrifice
acolytes.description: Once the Altar of Sacrifice is placed, the Acolytes also gain Power when passing Power thresholds while moving down on the Cult tracks.
acolytes.specialcost: Transforming any Terrain type (except Ice) by moving 3 steps down on a Cult track.

shapeshifters.name: Spectral Polestar
shapeshifters.description: When the Spectral Polestar is placed, the Shapeshifters may immediately and only once shift to any non-opponent Home Terrain at no cost.

riverwalkers.name: Floating Palace
riverwalkers.description: The Floating Palace must be placed on a River space that is directly adjacent to a Riverwalker Structure. It does not prevent other players from using that River space for expansion or indirect adjacency. Shipping works with the Floating Palace as with any other Structure.
